title: Rule (e) closes every form NEW-1-R1 listed, but an outside module can still obtain the `aegis` package (or import the execution package by a computed name) by roads no rule reads - `sys` handed on, a library call that returns a module, the import function taken out of builtins by a string, eval - and hold the Executor with all 863 architecture tests green
repro:
Rated high only because the rubric lists 'an Executor reference the architecture test misses'; every form is deliberate evasion, the fixer disclosed the pkgutil and __globals__ ones in its notes, and the lead may downgrade or accept it as a documented limit. Scratch copies under /tmp/aegis-verify3.KXhmTg (phase6 = today's tree + `from aegis.execution import Executor` appended to aegis/policy/engine.py).
(A) phase6, appended to aegis/cli/trace.py: `import pkgutil

_VENUE = pkgutil.resolve_name(__name__.partition(".")[0]).execution
_BASE = getattr(_VENUE, _VENUE.__all__[0])
` -> `pytest tests/test_policy_architecture.py` -> `863 passed in 14.26s`; `python -c "import aegis.cli.policy, aegis.cli.trace as trace; print(trace._VENUE.__name__, trace._BASE)"` -> `aegis.execution <class 'aegis.execution.base.Executor'>`.
(B) phase6, appended to aegis/cli/trace.py (which already imports sys): `import operator

_VENUE = operator.attrgetter("modules")(sys)[__name__.partition(".")[0]].execution
_BASE = getattr(_VENUE, _VENUE.__all__[0])
` -> `863 passed in 14.25s`, same print.
(C) TODAY's tree, dormant computed import of the execution package itself (a rule (a) miss), appended to aegis/cli/trace.py: `def _late():
    load = __builtins__["__imp" + "ort__"]
    return load(__name__.partition(".")[0] + ".exe" + "cution", None, None, ["base"])
` -> `863 passed in 14.20s`; `python -c "import aegis.cli.trace as trace; v = trace._late(); print(v.__name__, getattr(v, v.__all__[0]))"` -> `aegis.execution <class 'aegis.execution.base.Executor'>`.
(D) Probe /tmp/aegis-verify3.KXhmTg/alias_probe.py + residual.py (each form written as aegis/cli/zz_probe.py in the phase6 copy; five static rules, then `_run_imports(**_outside_job(extra=<assert zz_probe.HELD is the Executor class>))`). Each of these printed `MISSED ... (a)=False (b)=[] (c)=[] (d)=[] (e)=[] | runtime code=0 rogue={} failed={}` with the in-child assertion passing: `operator.attrgetter('modules')(sys)[computed]`; `sys.__getattribute__('modules')[computed]`; `getattr(trace.sys, 'modules')[computed]` (another module's `sys`); `pkgutil.resolve_name(computed)`; `__builtins__['__import__'](computed)`; `getattr(builtins, '__import__')(computed)`; `eval('__imp' + 'ort__')(computed)`; `importlib.util.find_spec(computed)` + `module_from_spec` + `exec_module` (not registered; see D3-R2-R1). Same result for the accepted, documented class 'what a policy module holds': `evaluate.__globals__`, `vars(inspect.getmodule(evaluate))`, `vars(engine)`. The 18 forms of the original item all print CAUGHT. The rule (e) docstring (lines 45-63) says 'no outside module may bind or obtain it at all' and names only `vars(engine)` as the limit, which overstates what is checked.
suggested_fix: Stop extending the static alias/handle chase; add a runtime 'who HOLDS it' check to the child script, which is route-independent. After the imports, for every module in sys.modules under `tree` and not under `allowed`, look at each value in vars(module) (one level into list/tuple/set/dict values): flag it when it is a module whose __name__ is under `tracked`, or its `__module__` (or its type's `__module__`) is under `tracked`; skip a package's own loaded submodule (`sys.modules.get(name + '.' + attr) is value`). Report as `holders` and exit 1. I prototyped exactly this in scratch (/tmp/aegis-verify3.KXhmTg/holders_patch.py, patched into scratch copies only): main run on today's tree, the phase6 copy and the paper.py copy -> `code 0 holders None`; every executed form above, the policy-namespace forms (`vars(engine)`, `__globals__`) and the rule (d)/(e) attribute forms -> `code 1 holders {'aegis.cli.zz_probe': ['VENUE', 'HELD']}`; the architecture file with the patch -> `2 failed, 861 passed`, both self-tests that today pin 'the runtime allows an outside module that holds the Executor' (test_an_outside_module_that_imports_a_policy_module_is_allowed[name-from-policy], test_a_reference_taken_off_an_attribute_is_the_static_rules_to_catch) - re-pin them as caught. Dormant code (form C, a function never called) stays static-only: either extend rules (a)/(e) by banning the means in outside modules - any use of `eval`/`exec`/`compile`/`__builtins__`/`builtins`/`pkgutil`/`importlib.util`/`runpy`/`pydoc`/`__globals__`, and the name `sys` used as anything but the object of a plain `sys.<attr>` access (grep on today's 47 outside modules: none of these occur; `sys` is only used as sys.argv/stderr/stdout/exit and sys.get_int_max_str_digits in a comment) - or say in the rule (e) docstring that deliberately obfuscated, never-executed code is beyond the tripwire, and reword 'may bind or obtain it at all' to what is actually read.

title: The runtime backstop sees a spec-based or file-path load of the execution package by an outside module only when it is the FIRST load; in Phase-6 order (a policy module loaded the package earlier) the run passes, and the new D3-R2 / D3-R3 self-tests pin the first-load order only
repro:
The fixer disclosed this (its note 1); the D3-R2 test docstring admits it; the module docstring still says 'what a module is charged with does not depend on who loaded the package first'. /tmp/aegis-verify3.KXhmTg/order_probe.py, toy tree, harness as shipped, rogue sources taken from the test class itself (SPEC_LOAD / FILE_LOAD, registered or not), in-child assertion that rogue.HELD is [Executor] from toy.execution.base. Without toy/cli/first.py: `[first-load] spec load, not registered: code 1 rogue {'toy.cli.rogue': ['toy.execution']}`, `[first-load] file-path load, not registered: code 1 rogue {'<unattributed>': ['toy.execution']}` (and the same for the registered variants). With toy/cli/first.py = `import toy.policy.engine`: `[phase-6 order] spec load, not registered: code 0 rogue {} failed {} | static (a..e) (False, [], [], [], [])`, `[phase-6 order] spec load, registered: code 0 rogue {} ... (e) ['<computed module>']`, `[phase-6 order] file-path load, not registered: code 0 rogue {} | static (False, [], [], [], [])`, `[phase-6 order] file-path load, registered: code 0 rogue {} ... (e) ['<computed module>']`. Real tree: phase6 copy with `import importlib.util as _u

_spec = _u.find_spec(__name__.partition(".")[0] + ".exe" + "cution")
_VENUE = _u.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(_VENUE)
_BASE = getattr(_VENUE, _VENUE.__all__[0])
` appended to aegis/cli/trace.py -> `863 passed in 14.23s` and `trace._BASE` is `<class 'aegis.execution.base.Executor'>`; the same lines appended in today's tree -> `12 failed, 851 passed` (first load: caught). In Phase 6 the walk imports aegis.cli.policy early, so almost every outside module runs in Phase-6 order.
suggested_fix: The 'who holds it' check proposed under NEW-1-R1-R1 closes this without more import hooks: with the prototype, the four Phase-6-order loads above each give `code 1 holders {'toy.cli.rogue': ['VENUE', 'HELD']}` and a clean outside module that imports the policy engine gives `code 0`. Then add the Phase-6-order variant (toy/cli/first.py present) as extra cases of test_a_load_from_a_spec_is_seen_by_the_finder_alone and test_a_load_nobody_was_seen_asking_for_is_nobodys_to_allow. If the lead prefers not to add the check, correct the module docstring sentence ('does not depend on who loaded the package first') to say it holds for imports, not for spec or file-path loads.

title: Nothing pins that the tree rule for (e) scans aegis/__init__.py AS the package: dropping `module=_module_name(path)` from the tree test leaves the suite green and the bare-name form unread
repro: Scratch copy of today's tree, line 1445 changed from `root_handles(_source(path), package=_package_of(path), module=_module_name(path))` to `root_handles(_source(path), package=_package_of(path))` -> static part of the file: `819 passed, 44 deselected` (no failure). With that change the item's aegis/__init__.py repro (`venue = execution` inside a function) is not flagged again: `root_handles(snippet, package='aegis', module='')` returns set() by the checker's own self-test at line 1316-1317. test_the_package_rule_reads_a_real_binding only asserts `_module_name(AEGIS_DIR / '__init__.py') == ROOT`, not that the tree rule passes it.
suggested_fix: Factor the tree rule's call into a helper, e.g. `def _handles_in(path): return root_handles(_source(path), package=_package_of(path), module=_module_name(path))`, use it in the parametrized tree test, and pin it once with a monkeypatched `_source` returning `"venue = execution\n"`: `_handles_in(AEGIS_DIR / '__init__.py') == {'execution'}` and `_handles_in(AEGIS_DIR / 'config.py') == set()`.

title: Rule (e) reads ANY attribute named `modules` as the module table, so honest code in an outside module fails the tree rule with the misleading message `holds ['<computed module>']`
suggested_fix: Keep it fail-closed but say what was read: report such a hit under its own label (e.g. `<attribute .modules>`) or put a sentence in the assertion message of test_no_module_outside_policy_holds_the_aegis_package_itself ('an attribute called .modules is read as sys.modules; rename it'), and add `self.modules[name]` to the flagged self-test list so the behaviour is a pinned decision rather than an accident.
